title: ruff target-version is py39 but the project requires >=3.10
description:
`pyproject.toml` has `[tool.ruff] target-version = "py39"` while `[project] requires-python = ">=3.10"`. Python 3.9 was dropped in v0.3.4 (end-of-life); the ruff setting was never updated.

## Why it matters

`target-version` tells ruff which syntax the codebase must remain compatible with. Pinned at `py39`, ruff's `UP` (pyupgrade) rules — which ARE enabled in `[tool.ruff.lint] select` — suppress every suggestion that would emit 3.10+ syntax. So the codebase is being held to a floor two versions below its actual one, and modernizations ruff would otherwise offer are invisible.

Harmless in the sense that nothing is broken. Wrong in the sense that the config states something untrue about the project.

## Expect this to cascade

Changing one line may surface a batch of `UP` findings — 3.10 brought `X | Y` union syntax, `match`, and parenthesized context managers, and `UP` will start proposing the union-syntax rewrites in particular. That is the actual work; the config edit is trivial.

Apply ruff's autofixes where they are safe and mechanical. If any suggested rewrite is NOT mechanical, or reduces clarity, leave it and say which — do not contort code to satisfy a lint rule. Note the codebase already uses `from __future__ import annotations` in places, which affects how annotation-related rules apply.
acceptance_criteria:
- `grep -n 'target-version' pyproject.toml` shows `py310`, matching `requires-python = ">=3.10"`.
- `uv run ruff check .` is clean at the new target.
- `uv run ruff format --check .` is clean.
- `uv run mypy src/` is clean (note `[tool.mypy] python_version` is separately set to 3.10 — confirm the two now agree).
- pytest passes on ALL FOUR supported versions, since the point is that 3.10 is the real floor: `for v in 3.10 3.11 3.12 3.13; do uv run --python $v --no-sync pytest -q || break; done`
- Any ruff suggestion deliberately NOT applied is listed in the bead notes with the reason.
close_reason: target-version now py310, matching requires-python and [tool.mypy] python_version. Surfaced UP035 (autofixed) and B905 in first_difference, where strict=False is correct because the bodies routinely differ in length; documented in the docstring. Verified across 3.10-3.13.

title: Enable hallucination checking for base36 IDs via a domain-term allowlist
description:
Hash-shaped references (`seeds-zq4x`) are currently invisible to hallucination checking. `find_id_refs` is called from `_validate_id_refs` with no `known_ids`, so `_is_id_ref` discards every non-numeric token before it is ever checked. An agent can cite a base36 ID that never existed and nothing notices — which is exactly the failure the check was built to catch, and base36 is the scheme every new ID uses (seeds-199).

Source: seeds-6hj5. **Depends on the bead-ID loading bead** — without it, enabling this flags all 16 legitimate bead references.

## The design (Ryan's, arrived at over three rounds of pushback — do not re-derive)

Check each candidate token against, in order:

1. **seed IDs** (exists today)
2. **bead IDs** (the prerequisite bead)
3. **a small allowlist of domain terms** (this bead)

Anything still unmatched is a hallucination — flag it.

The regex stays, but only to extract candidate tokens from free text. It performs no judgment; that was a red herring in the seed's earlier framing.

## Why an allowlist rather than a heuristic

"Cannot distinguish a hash from a word by shape" is true and does not matter, because you can enumerate the exceptions when there are eight of them. Measured across all 268 seeds — the complete set of `seeds-*` prose tokens in the project's entire history:

```
seeds-marketplace    seeds-cli       seeds-native    seeds-tool
seeds-generated      seeds-level     seeds-like      seeds-side
```

These are real domain vocabulary, not contrived: `seeds-marketplace` is the Claude Code plugin marketplace, `seeds-cli` is the PyPI name under consideration in seeds-95. Seed the allowlist with exactly these eight.

**Rejected alternative — do not implement:** a length/entropy heuristic (require a digit, reject dictionary words). An all-digit suffix is a valid hash and a 4-letter English word is valid base36, so it both misses and false-positives. seeds-6hj5 records this as a trap.

## Note: this makes the check STRICTER

Today hash-shaped hallucinations pass silently. After this they are caught. That is the point — but it means seeds whose bodies were written under the looser rule may now fail validation. Run the new check across the existing 268-seed database before shipping and confirm it reports zero unknowns; if it reports any, they are either real hallucinations worth fixing or allowlist entries worth adding. Record the outcome in the bead notes.

## Where the allowlist lives

Prefer a module-level constant with a comment explaining what it is and when to add to it — a future reader must understand these are prose, not IDs. Making it user-configurable is NOT required; revisit only if the list grows past ~20 entries. Maintenance is roughly one addition every few months, and the failure mode is a clear error naming exactly what to add.
acceptance_criteria:
- A reference to a nonexistent hash-shaped ID is now REJECTED: in a temp SEEDS_DIR, `seeds create -t "t" -c "see seeds-zq4x"` exits non-zero and names `seeds-zq4x`. (This currently succeeds — verify it fails after the change.)
- Every one of the 8 allowlisted terms is accepted: creating a seed whose body contains `seeds-marketplace`, `seeds-cli`, `seeds-native`, `seeds-tool`, `seeds-generated`, `seeds-level`, `seeds-like`, `seeds-side` succeeds without `--allow-unknown-refs`.
- Real bead references still pass (the prerequisite bead's behavior is not regressed): a body citing `seeds-230` succeeds.
- Real seed references still pass: a body citing an existing seed ID succeeds.
- Running the validator over all 268 existing seeds reports zero unknown references — script it, paste the output, and record any allowlist additions in the bead notes.
- `--allow-unknown-refs` still overrides everything.
- Tests cover: hallucinated hash rejected, allowlisted term accepted, real bead accepted, real seed accepted.
- `uv run pytest` green; `uv run ruff check .` clean; `uv run mypy src/` clean.
notes:
Pre-ship sweep of the real .seeds/seeds.jsonl (270 seeds, 100 beads, read-only: JSONL parsed directly, validation logic called in-process, no mutating commands).

RESULT: 16 distinct prefixed tokens resolved to neither a seed nor a bead. ZERO were hallucinations.

The 8 the bead measured were confirmed and seeded into PROSE_REF_ALLOWLIST: marketplace, cli, native, tool, generated, level, like, side.

The sweep found 5 MORE word-shaped prose terms the measurement missed (each occurs once, in seeds written after or outside the measured set). All are the same category as the original 8, so they were added to the allowlist, bringing it to 13 (bead threshold for revisiting is ~20):
  - experiment  (seeds-199: "`seeds-experiment`-style IDs")
  - recent      (seeds-87: the `seeds recent` primitive)
  - specific    (seeds-74.2.2: "a seeds-specific phrase")
  - sweep       (seeds-74.2.2: the proposed /seeds-sweep slash command)
  - whatever    (seeds-6hj5: placeholder inside a quoted design discussion)

3 residual tokens were deliberately NOT allowlisted, because they are ID-shaped, not prose -- design write-ups quoting a fabricated example ID. Allowlisting an ID-shaped token would blind the check to that ID forever, inverting the point of the list:
  - seeds-7.1  (seeds-140 content: "e.g., seeds-1, seeds-7.1") -- PRE-EXISTING. It is numeric, so today/main already flags it; the baseline sweep on main reports this same 1 hit. Not a regression from this bead.
  - seeds-k3n  (seeds-199 content: "a 3-4 char id like `seeds-k3n`") -- the ONLY new failure this bead introduces across the whole corpus.
  - seeds-8su  (seeds-199 RESOLUTION field) -- out of the validated surface entirely: create validates [title, content] and update validates [title, content, append]; no command validates resolution.

So the post-change sweep over the validated surface reports 2 unknowns, not 0: one pre-existing (seeds-7.1) and one new (seeds-k3n). Both are documentation prose quoting example IDs; the honest fix is in those two seed bodies (write them as placeholders, or use --allow-unknown-refs when next editing them), not in the allowlist. The seed bodies were NOT edited -- the sweep was required to be read-only.
Design picks not pinned by the bead:

1. find_id_refs -> find_id_ref_candidates. The bead says the regex "performs no judgment", and _validate_id_refs was its only production caller. Rather than add a second extractor and leave find_id_refs as dead-but-tested code, the function was renamed and its known_ids parameter dropped: it now returns every whole-word <prefix>-... token and the caller judges. _is_id_ref keeps its known_ids logic, still used by rewrite_id_refs / iter_id_ref_snippets on the prefix-rename path.

2. Allowlist stored as BARE SUFFIXES (frozenset {"cli", "native", ...}), not full "seeds-cli" tokens, so a project with any other prefix inherits the vocabulary. Verified: in a csc-prefixed temp store, "a csc-native workflow with csc-cli" is accepted while "csc-zq4x" is rejected. A test asserts no entry contains a hyphen, so a future prefixed entry (which would silently never match) fails loudly.

3. Error message now names the constant to add to: "If one is prose rather than an ID, add its suffix to PROSE_REF_ALLOWLIST in seeds/models.py."
close_reason: base36 refs now validated: seed IDs -> bead IDs -> 13-entry bare-suffix prose allowlist. Sweep of 270 seeds + 100 beads found 16 unmatched, zero hallucinations. AC predicted zero residuals; actual is 2 (seeds-7.1 pre-existing/numeric, seeds-k3n the one new hit) — both ID-shaped examples in prose, deliberately not allowlisted, decision recorded on seeds-6hj5.

title: Emit compact JSON from seeds suggest --json (no indent, tight separators)
description:
`seeds suggest --json` pretty-prints with `indent=2`, even though the flag's own help text reads **"Emit JSON for agent piping"**. The single place seeds pretty-prints JSON is the one place whose stated purpose is machine consumption. Make it compact.

Source: seeds-d773 (deliberation). Related: seeds-142.1 (originated `seeds suggest` and asked "JSON output mode for agent piping?"), seeds-137 / seeds-138 (output-economy family).

## Motivation

JSON emitted for an agent is JSON an LLM pays tokens to read. Indentation is pure overhead on that path. Measured on a real `seeds suggest` result: 406 bytes pretty vs 292 compact — **28.1% smaller**.

## Locked decisions — do NOT re-open

- **Always compact. No `--pretty` flag, no config option.** Ryan's call, verbatim: *"maybe we don't even need that. Maybe we just want it compacted at all times. And someone can just run it through JQ when they want a pretty printed version."* Rationale: `jq` is the universal pretty-printer and already installed everywhere we care about; a flag is surface area to document, test, and keep working in exchange for what one pipe already does.
- **Do NOT make it TTY-conditional** (compact when piped, pretty when interactive). This was considered and rejected: output that changes shape depending on whether stdout is a terminal is exactly what surprises someone debugging a pipeline, and it contradicts the "one predictable machine format" intent above.
- **Use `separators=(",", ":")`, not merely dropping `indent`.** Python's `json.dumps` keeps `", "` / `": "` padding by default. Measured: `indent=2` 599 bytes -> no-indent 453 -> tight separators 415. Dropping indent alone leaves ~8% on the table.

## Scope fence — exactly one line changes

`src/seeds/cli.py:472`, inside the `suggest` command:

```python
click.echo(_json.dumps(payload, indent=2))
```

becomes the tight-separator form. That is the whole production change.

**Do NOT touch these** (audited 2026-08-10, all four are correct as-is):
- `src/seeds/export.py:103` — the JSONL export. It uses default separators and is NOT maximally compact, and that is deliberate. Compacting it would rewrite every line of a git-tracked 520KB file (permanently muddying `git log -p` / `git blame` on the whole deliberation history) to save 1.8%. It is a sync artifact, not agent-facing output. seeds-d773 records this decision — do not "finish the job" here.
- `src/seeds/db.py:424,466` — tags serialized into SQLite. Internal storage; nothing reads it as text.
- `src/seeds/web.py` — its three Flask routes render HTML templates and emit no JSON at all.
- Any `json.loads` call site — those are reads, not output.

## Also update the help text

The `--json` flag's help currently reads `"Emit JSON for agent piping"`. Make it state the format is compact, so nobody is surprised or files this as a bug — e.g. `"Emit compact JSON for agent piping (pipe through jq to read it)"`.
acceptance_criteria:
- `uv run seeds suggest "nix" --json` output contains NO newline except a single trailing one: `uv run seeds suggest "nix" --json | wc -l` returns 1.
- Output contains no `", "` or `": "` separator padding: `uv run seeds suggest "nix" --json | grep -cE '", "|": "'` returns 0.
- Output is still valid JSON: `uv run seeds suggest "nix" --json | jq -e 'type == "array"'` exits 0.
- Field content is unchanged — same keys as before: `uv run seeds suggest "nix" --json | jq -e '.[0] | has("id") and has("title") and has("status") and has("tags") and has("snippet") and has("score")'` exits 0 (when there is at least one result).
- `grep -n 'indent=2' src/seeds/cli.py` returns no match.
- `.seeds/seeds.jsonl` is byte-identical to before the change (`git diff --stat .seeds/seeds.jsonl` shows nothing beyond ordinary seed edits) — the export was NOT touched.
- `grep -c 'compact' src/seeds/cli.py` >= 1 (the --json help text mentions the format).
- A test covers the compact shape so it cannot silently regress to pretty-printing.
- Full suite green: `uv run pytest`.
close_reason: suggest --json now emits compact JSON (separators=(',',':')); 21% smaller on a live query; regression test verified to fail against indent=2

title: Flaky test: test_rename_prefix_no_rewrite_bodies fails intermittently under full-suite runs
description:
`tests/test_cli.py::TestRenamePrefixCommand::test_rename_prefix_no_rewrite_bodies` fails intermittently. Observed once during a pre-commit hook run on main; did NOT reproduce on a subsequent full-suite run (433 passed) or on 5/5 isolated runs of the test alone.

## Observed failure

```
    result = cli_runner.invoke(main, ["show", hub_id])
    # Reference is now stale — the seeds-1 in body wasn't rewritten.
>   assert "see seeds-1" in result.output
E   assert 'see seeds-1' in "Error: Seed 'seeds-060' not found.\n"
E    +  where "Error: Seed 'seeds-060' not found.\n" = <Result SystemExit(1)>
tests/test_cli.py:281
```

## Likely cause

The test hardcodes a seed at id `seeds-1`, then CLI-creates a second ("hub") whose id comes from `next_id()`. Since the switch to base36 hash IDs (seeds-tek / seeds-mlj, grandfathering sequential), the generated id varies per run — here it was `seeds-060`.

The assertion depends on `show hub_id` still resolving AFTER `rename-prefix demo` has run. That only holds if `show` can still resolve the pre-rename id. So the test is probably sensitive to which id shape `next_id()` produces — i.e. whether the generated id looks sequential (grandfathered path) or base36-hash (new path), and whether the rename/lookup logic treats those differently.

That would make this not merely a flaky test but a **real inconsistency in `rename-prefix` / `show` id resolution across the two id shapes** — worth determining which before "fixing the test."

## Do NOT

- Do not paper over it by loosening the assertion or adding a retry. Determine first whether the flake is in the test's assumption or in `rename-prefix`/`show` behavior. If it's the latter, this bead becomes a production bug and the test is correct as written.

## Reproduction hint

Isolated runs pass. Reproduce by running the full suite repeatedly, or seed `next_id()` deterministically to force a base36-hash id (vs a grandfathered sequential one) and run the test under each.
acceptance_criteria:
- Root cause identified and stated in the bead notes: test-assumption bug vs. real `rename-prefix`/`show` id-resolution inconsistency.
- A test exists that deterministically exercises BOTH id shapes (grandfathered sequential and base36 hash) through `rename-prefix` followed by `show`.
- `uv run pytest` passes 20 consecutive full-suite runs (`for i in $(seq 20); do uv run pytest -q || break; done`).
- If a production bug was found, the fix is in src/ and not only in tests/.
notes:
DIRECTION FROM RYAN (2026-07-26): "fix test and understand we're doing base36 going forward."

Base36 hash IDs are the standard for all NEW ids (resolved in seeds-199, shipped via seeds-tek + seeds-mlj). Sequential ids are grandfathered legacy, not a co-equal scheme — do not add new machinery to keep sequential generation alive.

BUT both shapes genuinely coexist in real databases and must both keep working. This very repo proves it: sequential ids (seeds-95, seeds-112, seeds-154) sit alongside base36 hash ids (seeds-gf69, seeds-0y4, seeds-80g) in the same .seeds database. So `rename-prefix` and `show` must resolve BOTH correctly — the acceptance criterion covering both shapes stands.

Framing: treat base36 as the normal path and sequential as legacy data that must not break. If the root cause turns out to be that `rename-prefix`/`show` mishandles one shape, fix the production code — do not loosen the test.
ROOT CAUSE (2026-07-26): production bug in rename-prefix, not just a bad test assumption.

Database.rename_prefix decided which IDs belonged to the old prefix with a
numeric-only shape test written back when every ID was sequential:

    try:
        int(top[len(old_lead):])   # 'seeds-7' -> 7
    except ValueError:
        continue                    # skipped

A base36 hash suffix is drawn from [0-9a-z], so ~2% of length-3 hashes are
all digits. 'seeds-060' therefore parsed as a number and WAS renamed, while
'seeds-k3n7' was not. Same ID shape, opposite outcome, decided by the random
content of the hash — that is the whole flake. The observed failure ('Error:
Seed seeds-060 not found') was the hub seed getting renamed to demo-060 and
'show seeds-060' then missing it; the test passed on every run where the
minted hash happened to contain a letter.

Consequences beyond the flake: 'seeds rename-prefix demo' on a real database
left it in a split-prefix state — demo-1 and demo-060 renamed, seeds-k3n7
stranded — while get_prefix() reported 'demo', so new IDs minted as demo-*
against mostly seeds-* data. That contradicts the command's own contract
('rewrite all seed IDs to use it'). This repo would hit it today: seeds-95
and seeds-112 sit alongside seeds-gf69 and seeds-0y4.

FIX (src/, per the bead): both schemes rename, deterministically.
- idgen.is_hash_suffix(suffix, min_len, max_len): base36 chars within the
  configured adaptive-length window. New helper, no new ID generation.
- rename_prefix now matches suffix.isdigit() (grandfathered sequential, any
  length) OR is_hash_suffix(...) (base36, the standard). 'seeds-experiment'
  still isn't renamed — 10 chars exceeds max_hash_length, so the original
  guard's purpose is preserved.
- Body refs had the same numeric-only assumption (_id_ref_pattern matched
  \\d+ only). Renaming hash IDs without this would strand every mention of
  them, so the pattern now matches base36 and rewrite_id_refs/find_id_refs/
  iter_id_ref_snippets take a known_ids set: numeric refs rewrite
  unconditionally (preserves refs to deleted seeds), hash-shaped refs only
  when they name a real seed. Nothing can tell 'seeds-related' from a hash
  by shape, so database membership is the only sound test.

DESIGN PICK (2-way, documented): make rename-prefix rename BOTH shapes rather
than deterministically skip hash IDs. Skipping is unsound (all-digit hashes
are indistinguishable from sequential IDs) and would make rename-prefix a
near no-op now that base36 is the standard. Consequence: the two CLI tests
that asserted a hash-ID seed survives rename-prefix encoded the bug; they now
assert the seed is renamed and that 'show' resolves the new ID. No assertion
was loosened — the stale-body-ref assertion is preserved verbatim.

VERIFICATION: 20/20 consecutive full-suite runs green (457 passed each). Both
new deterministic tests fail against pre-fix src (verified by stashing the
src changes), so they are real regression tests rather than the flake's luck.
close_reason: root cause was a production bug: rename_prefix used a numeric-only int() test, renaming all-digit base36 hashes but skipping alphanumeric ones; now matches both schemes, body-ref rewriting gated on known_ids

description:
Optional follow-on to the feedback-skill spike. Once the install mechanism is proven (seeds-dn7 passes), adding a second prompt-macro skill is a small repeat.

Reference deliberation: seeds-152.4 (this skill's design rationale and resolution of the workflow-engine-vs-macro tension).

This bead is stretch scope. Only do it if seeds-dn7 has passed and there's time. If the prompt-macro framing turns out to be insufficient in practice, file a new seed rather than expanding scope here.

## File to create

src/seeds/plugin/claude-plugin/skills/seeds-to-beads/SKILL.md

## Exact content

```markdown
---
name: seeds-to-beads
description: Use when the user has reached agreement on a feature after a deliberation captured in seeds, and wants the relevant seeds turned into a set of beads (tasks) executable by a Sonnet-based agent.
---

# Seeds → beads conversion

The user has deliberated a feature using seeds and now wants the agreed scope handed off as beads for execution by a Sonnet-based agent. Convert the relevant seeds into a set of beads following these principles:

- Separate actionable scope (decisions, agreed paths) from context (concerns, observations, refinements). Beads represent work; seeds carry the deliberation.
- Decompose into small, self-contained beads. Each bead should be doable in one focused effort.
- Pre-write content. If a bead requires a file with specific content, include the content verbatim in the bead description so the executing agent doesn't have to re-design.
- Acceptance criteria must be mechanically checkable (file exists, command exits 0, output contains string X).
- Set explicit dependencies between beads.
- Cite seed IDs for deliberation context the executing agent might need.
- After creating beads, land the plane: commit unstaged work into a clean tree.

Do this conversion once when invoked. Do not adopt the conversion behavior as a default for subsequent turns.
```

## Plugin version bump

Bump the version in both manifest files (src/seeds/plugin/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json and src/seeds/plugin/claude-plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json) from 0.1.0 to 0.2.0 so `claude plugin update` recognizes the change.
acceptance_criteria:
1. File exists: src/seeds/plugin/claude-plugin/skills/seeds-to-beads/SKILL.md
2. File contains the YAML frontmatter with `name: seeds-to-beads`
3. File contains the load-bearing principles (separation of action vs context, content templates, mechanical acceptance criteria, dependencies, seed IDs, land-the-plane)
4. File contains the "do this once when invoked" self-scope constraint (per seeds-151.2 and seeds-152.4)
5. Both manifest files have version bumped from 0.1.0 to 0.2.0
6. Running `seeds skills install` (or update) picks up the new skill
7. File length under 30 lines
close_reason: Added seeds-to-beads SKILL.md + bumped plugin manifests to 0.2.0

title: Add README section describing the feedback skill and 'seeds skills install'
description:
Brief documentation update so future adopters discover the feedback skill exists. Not exhaustive — a section, not a chapter.

Reference: the feedback skill (seeds-0h8), install command (seeds-9q6), deliberation context (seeds-152, seeds-152.3).

## What to add to README.md

A new section, probably titled "Claude Code Skills" or "Companion Skills", placed near the existing "Commands" or "Deploy to Global CLI" sections. Suggested content:

```markdown
## Claude Code Skills

seeds ships a small set of skills for use with Claude Code, distributed as a local plugin. After installing the seeds CLI, run:

\`\`\`bash
seeds skills install
\`\`\`

This registers the bundled marketplace and installs the `seeds` plugin under the `seeds:*` namespace.

### Available skills

- **`seeds:feedback`** — frames the next user message as feedback on the agent's prior turn and invites the agent to follow up with its own questions, comments, or criticisms. Useful during deliberation when you want the agent to push back rather than just execute.

Run `seeds skills install` again after `uv tool upgrade seeds` to pick up updated skill content.
```

Adjust phrasing as needed to match the rest of the README's voice.

## What NOT to do

- Don't expand into a full design treatise. Brief.
- Don't add more skills to the list than actually ship in this spike. (Only `seeds:feedback` ships in this round.)

title: Tighten conn typing on Database migration helpers
description:
The \`_migrate_add_resolution\` / \`_migrate_add_config\` (and now \`_apply_body_id_rewrites\`) methods use \`conn = self._conn\` and then call \`conn.execute(...)\` without narrowing the Optional[Connection] type. Pre-existing pattern; mypy flags 7 errors.

Fix: route through \`self._get_conn()\` so the type narrows, or add an explicit assertion. The runtime behavior is fine — these methods are only called after \`_get_conn\` populated \`self._conn\` — but the type hint should reflect that.

## Acceptance
- \`uv run mypy src/seeds/\` reports 0 errors in db.py
- All 285+ tests still pass
- No runtime behavior change
close_reason: Pulled conn out as method parameter on _migrate_add_resolution/_migrate_add_config; annotated get_config return. mypy now clean: 0 errors in 7 source files.
